chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said:

When it was the day of the conquest of Mecca, a tent of black hair was pitched for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) at Al-Abtah. Then water was poured upon it from a bowl in which the traces of dough were seen. Then he determined the Qiblah in the forenoon, so he bowed in eight Raka'at. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had not bowed in these before that, nor (did he) afterwards.
ai.seo_question: What specific prayer did the Prophet perform after the conquest of Mecca?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi highlights the Prophet's (SAWW) unique gratitude ritual upon the conquest of Mecca, where he performed eight Raka'at at Al-Abtah with a specific ablution from a bowl bearing dough traces. Shia scholars often cite this as evidence for the validity of offering optional prayers at specific times and locations, emphasizing the spiritual significance of the forenoon (Dhuha) prayer in commemorating divine victories.
